package: @astryxdesign/cli

## StyleX for your own code

Only needed when you write your own StyleX (`stylex.create()`) or swizzle a component (`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 swizzle <Component>`), which copies its StyleX source into your app. The plain path already supports `xstyle` overrides — this path is for your own StyleX code. Some built-in page templates also use StyleX for layout; if you scaffold one and see "Unexpected stylex.create call at runtime", add the compiler plugin for your bundler below.

Install:
```bash
npm install @astryxdesign/core @stylexjs/stylex @astryxdesign/theme-neutral
```

globals.css:
```css
@import "@astryxdesign/core/reset.css";
@import "@astryxdesign/core/astryx.css";
@import "@astryxdesign/theme-neutral/theme.css";
```

Keep `astryx.css`: Astryx component styles always come from the prebuilt stylesheets. Point the StyleX compiler at your own source only, never at `node_modules/@astryxdesign`. Add the plugin for your bundler:

Bundler                  | Plugin                                           
------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------
Webpack                  | @stylexjs/webpack-plugin                         
Vite / Rollup            | @stylexjs/rollup-plugin                          
Babel (any)              | @stylexjs/babel-plugin + @stylexjs/postcss-plugin
Next.js (keep next/font) | @stylexswc/nextjs-plugin                         

If a swizzled component fails at runtime with a `stylex.create` error, the app is missing a StyleX compiler: see the StyleX Build Setup section of `npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs styling/tokens-and-setup`.

`npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 swizzle <Component>` writes an `astryx-swizzle.json` marker into an output folder it owns (one the copy creates, an empty one, or one it marked before); every module under that folder then compiles as Astryx source, so keep copies in a folder of their own, such as the default `components/astryx`. For a folder that already holds other files it writes no marker and says how to add one by hand. With `@astryxdesign/build`'s Babel, PostCSS and Vite integrations, or `withAstryx()` under webpack, a copy under that folder compiles into `astryx-base`, below `astryx-theme`, so theme component overrides reach it as they reach the package component. Under Turbopack, and with the stock StyleX plugins above, a copy's rules land in your own styles, above `astryx-theme`, and theme component overrides do not reach it.
